keyFacts.claim: navigator.storage.persist()/persisted() are Baseline Widely Available (since Dec 2021, Safari 15.2+), secure-context only, and persist() is not available in workers

Best practice: call persist() when first saving data the user cares about, wrapped in a user gesture, after checking persisted(); Chrome never prompts (silently grants based on site engagement / PWA install / notification permission) while Firefox shows a prompt
Chrome is significantly more likely to grant persist() after the PWA is installed, so re-requesting after the appinstalled event is worthwhile

Standard static-site IndexedDB backup pattern is getAll per store -> JSON envelope -> Blob -> <a download> click; import via <input type=file> -> JSON.parse -> readwrite transaction; widely-used reference implementations exist

risks: ts-fsrs 6.0 is imminent (6.0.0-beta.7 on npm, main branch is already the v6 monorepo, npm activity as recent as Aug 18 2026): pin ^5.4.1; v6 removes Card.elapsed_days and may reshape packages (@open-spaced-repetition/binding appears for optimizer). Persist raw Card objects, not derived fields, so a future migration is a data no-op.
Card.elapsed_days is deprecated in 5.4.1 — avoid using it anywhere (removed in 6.0).
f.get_retrievability() returns a formatted STRING ('100.00%') unless you pass false as the 3rd argument — easy to feed into arithmetic by mistake.

Chrome may silently DENY navigator.storage.persist() for a fresh low-engagement site — do not treat a false return as an error; retry after PWA install (appinstalled event) and surface export/backup as the reliable safety net.

Safari's storage eviction remains the most aggressive (ITP can clear script-writable storage for rarely-visited non-installed sites even though persist() is supported since 15.2) — not re-verified in this session; encourage Home-Screen install and periodic JSON export for Safari users.

JSON round-trip silently turns Dates into strings: the 'cards' store's by-due index needs real Date keys, so the import path must revive due/last_review (snippet does); forgetting this breaks getDueCards() ordering while ts-fsrs itself keeps working (masks the bug).

idb upgrade callbacks cannot open their own transactions — data migrations must use the versionchange transaction argument, and a second tab holding an old connection will block upgrades (handle the blocking() callback, e.g. reload).

The 'settings' store uses out-of-line keys, so getAll() alone loses the keys — export must pair getAllKeys() with getAll() (handled in snippet); naive per-store getAll() backup code found in blog posts gets this wrong.

Multi-store readwrite restore clears stores before writing — if the import file is corrupt mid-way the tx aborts and rolls back (good), but validate the envelope before starting to avoid a confusing failed-import UX.

keyFacts.claim: A static Astro site deploys to Vercel with zero configuration and NO adapter; @astrojs/vercel is only needed for SSR/ISR or Vercel features like Web Analytics and Image Optimization.

Current npm versions (2026-08-18): astro latest = 7.2.3, @astrojs/vercel latest = 11.0.6; the adapter has a single entry point `@astrojs/vercel` (the /static and /serverless entrypoints no longer exist).

Vercel's Astro framework preset auto-detects buildCommand `astro build`, outputDirectory `dist`, and its defaultRoutes automatically set `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on `/_astro/(.*)` and `/assets/(.*)` — hashed assets are long-cached even without vercel.json.

Vercel's default Cache-Control for responses is `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, and Vercel's own vercel.json docs example sets exactly that header on a `/service-worker.js` source — the sanctioned pattern for keeping sw.js un-cached in browsers.

Production-branch default order for new projects is main → master → repo default, so a repo whose default branch is `master` gets `master` as production automatically; it can be pinned under Settings → Environments → Production → Branch Tracking. Every push to any other branch creates a preview deployment.

Root Directory (e.g. `app/`) is a dashboard-only setting (Settings → Build and Deployment → Root Directory) — vercel.json has NO rootDirectory property; vercel.json must live inside the configured root directory (app/vercel.json), and the build cannot access files outside it unless 'Include source files outside of the Root Directory' is enabled (default-on since Aug 2020).

Hobby tier limits relevant to a static PWA: 100 GB/month Fast Data Transfer, up to 1M Edge Requests/month, 100 deployments/day, 1 concurrent build, 45-min max build, 2 vCPU/8 GB build container, 200 projects, 50 domains/project; overages pause the resource (no billing); Hobby is restricted to non-commercial personal use.

Deployment Protection (Vercel Authentication, Standard Protection scope) has been enabled BY DEFAULT for new projects since Nov 2023; on Hobby it protects preview deployments and generated deployment URLs but production domains always remain public (protecting production requires Pro/Enterprise).

Vercel Authentication on previews redirects unauthenticated requests to Vercel SSO login, which breaks service-worker registration and PWA testing on preview URLs; disable it per-project at Settings → Deployment Protection (or API `"ssoProtection": null`), or bypass with Shareable Links / the protection-bypass automation header.
keyFacts.source: https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-protection/methods-to-protect-deployments/vercel-authentication (SSO redirect behavior documented; SW breakage is the direct consequence)

keyFacts.claim: Hobby teams cannot connect a Vercel project to a Git repository owned by a GitHub organization (personal-account repos only).

vercel.json `headers.source` patterns are path-to-regexp style (`/(.*)`, `/:path*`, named params with regex), case-sensitive, match pathname excluding querystring; each header/redirect/rewrite rule counts toward the routes-per-deployment limit; `s-maxage` and CDN-Cache-Control values in vercel.json are consumed by Vercel's CDN and stripped from client responses.
Framework preset defaultRoutes and custom vercel.json headers coexist (the recommended config restates the _astro immutable rule so correctness does not depend on merge-order details).
keyFacts.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel/vercel/main/packages/frameworks/src/frameworks.ts (defaultRoutes use continue:true) — exact merge precedence not explicitly documented

risks: Vercel Authentication is ON by default for new projects: preview-URL service-worker registration and mobile install testing will fail with an SSO redirect until you disable it (Settings → Deployment Protection) or use a bypass — verify with `curl -sI <preview>/sw.js` expecting 200, not 30x to vercel.com/sso

Vercel deploys are atomic: after a new production deploy, OLD hashed /_astro/* URLs 404. A service worker must precache everything it needs at install time (full precache manifest), not lazily, or offline users mid-upgrade will hit failed fetches

Hobby plan is limited to non-commercial personal use (fair-use guidelines) and hard-pauses on overage (100 GB fast data transfer, 1M edge requests/month) with no paid-overflow option — a traffic spike takes the site down until the 30-day window resets

Root Directory cannot be set in vercel.json — if it is not set to `app` in the dashboard (or at import time), Vercel builds the repo root and the deploy fails or ships the wrong content; also remember vercel.json goes in app/, not the repo root

Vercel's docs page for Astro (vercel.com/docs/frameworks/astro) still shows the pre-v8 adapter API (@astrojs/vercel/serverless, output:'hybrid') — following it verbatim against @astrojs/vercel 11 / Astro 7 will not work; use Astro's integration docs instead
Do not use vercel.json `rewrites` for URL rewriting with Astro — Vercel documents it as unsupported/inconsistent for Astro projects (relevant only if SPA-style fallback routing is ever considered)
If the GitHub repo is ever moved into a GitHub organization, the Hobby project loses the git connection (org repos require Pro)

vercel.json `headers.source` is case-sensitive and matches the pathname exactly — a sw.js rule will not cover a service worker emitted under a different name/path (e.g. by a PWA plugin that outputs /service-worker.js), so keep the rule in sync with the actual SW filename

Cloning JPerm's UX too literally (exact shortcuts, labels, layout) could read as a rip-off in the cubing community; borrow the interaction model, not the skin.
Vote counts and alg orderings on SpeedCubeDB change over time; if Cubepath curates 'community-preferred' algs from it, snapshot and attribute rather than hotlink.

keyFacts.claim: iOS 26/Safari 26: every site added to the Home Screen opens as a web app by default ('Open as Web App' toggle, on by default); there are zero installability requirements (no manifest or service worker needed).
Safari 26.0 supports SVG icons and data-URL icons everywhere icons are used, including favicons; manifest icons are used when defined.
On iOS, a <link rel="apple-touch-icon"> overrides manifest icons for the Home Screen icon when both are present (manifest icons honored since iOS 15.4).

beforeinstallprompt is still not supported in Safari or Firefox (Chromium-only, non-Baseline, spec status 'Manifest Incubations'); iOS install UX must be a manual hint: Share button then Add to Home Screen.
iOS/WebKit storage: origin quota up to ~60% of disk in browser apps and Home Screen web apps (15% for in-app web views); overall cap 80%/20%; storage.estimate() supported since Safari 17.
navigator.storage.persist() in Safari shows no prompt; WebKit grants it based on heuristics such as the site running as a Home Screen web app, and persistent origins are skipped by idle eviction.

Safari's 7-day script-writable-storage eviction applies to Safari browsing; Home Screen web apps have their own days-of-use counter that resets on use — Apple: 'We do not expect the first-party in such a web application to have its website data deleted.'

Chrome install criteria for beforeinstallprompt: HTTPS, not installed, user clicked page at least once ever plus 30s total viewing, manifest with name/short_name, icons incl. 192px and 512px, start_url, display in {fullscreen, standalone, minimal-ui, window-controls-overlay}, prefer_related_applications absent or false. Service worker is not listed as a requirement (doc updated 2024-09-19).
Chrome removed the service-worker+fetch-handler requirement for menu install in Chrome 108 (Android) / 112 (desktop), providing a default offline page for sites without one.
Set an explicit manifest 'id'; Chrome 96+ otherwise computes it from start_url (freezing start_url); verify the Computed App Id in DevTools > Application > Manifest.
Use separate icon entries for purpose 'any' and 'maskable' (combining discouraged: maskable-as-any adds padding); maskable safe zone is a circle of 40% of icon width radius, outer 10% may be cropped.
purpose: 'monochrome' is in the W3C manifest spec (alpha channel used as mask over a solid fill) but has little consuming browser UI today — optional.

Workbox/vite-plugin-pwa precache defaults: globPatterns '**/*.{js,css,html}' (wasm NOT included) and maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes 2 MiB (larger files skipped; vite-plugin-pwa >=0.20.2 fails the build on that warning) — both must be overridden to precache wasm.
cubing.js latest is 0.63.3, pure ESM, module-workers-only; known Vite friction with its dynamically imported search worker/wasm — recommended workaround is optimizeDeps.exclude: ['cubing'].
Vite's import.meta.url/worker URL rewriting breaks for workers inside pre-bundled or library dependencies (404s / build hangs), affecting packages like cubing.js.
Dynamic import() is disallowed inside service worker scripts (static imports in module SWs are fine).
Safari 26.6 fixed service worker registrations with missing main scripts not being auto-unregistered, which had blocked re-registering new service workers.

@vite-pwa/astro latest is 1.2.0 (uses vite-plugin-pwa ^1.2.0); astro latest on npm is 7.2.3 — the peer range read from the registry only lists Astro ^1.6–^5, so compatibility with Astro 7 must be verified at install time.
Chrome desktop (~124+) offers menu-based 'Install page as app' for any website, giving a manual install path even when the prompt criteria are unmet.

risks: @vite-pwa/astro 1.2.0's peer range (as read from the registry) tops out at Astro ^5 while npm's latest astro is 7.2.3 — verify peer compatibility (or pin Astro accordingly / check for a newer @vite-pwa/astro) before scaffolding.

firt.dev's apple-touch-icon-overrides-manifest-icons precedence was last verified for iOS 15.4–17 (page dated June 2023); re-test on an iOS 26 device — keep apple-touch-icon identical to the manifest icon art so precedence doesn't matter.

Non-installed Safari users are still subject to the 7-day script-writable-storage eviction; user progress stored only in IndexedDB can vanish for tab users — call navigator.storage.persist() early and nudge Home Screen install.

cubing.js resolves its search worker and wasm at runtime via dynamic import/import.meta.url; if the emitted URLs are not in the precache manifest (or covered by a runtime caching route), the app breaks offline only when scramble/solve is first used — add an explicit offline E2E test for scramble generation.

Workbox will silently skip any asset over maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes (2 MiB default) from precache — with vite-plugin-pwa >=0.20.2 this becomes a build error, but if globPatterns omit .wasm there is no error at all, just a broken offline app.

WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming requires Content-Type: application/wasm; spot-check Vercel's header for .wasm (it normally serves it correctly, but this was not verified in this research) or use a non-streaming fallback.

Chrome's engagement heuristic (click + 30s viewing) means beforeinstallprompt often fires late or never in short first sessions — design the install button to appear whenever the deferred event exists, not on page load.

Safari never fires beforeinstallprompt and Chrome's criteria/heuristics are non-contractual and may shift again (they changed in 108/112 and docs were rewritten in 2024) — never hard-fail UX on prompt availability.

Older iOS versions in the wild (pre-26) still require the manifest/meta configuration for standalone behavior — keep display: standalone and apple-touch-icon rather than relying on iOS 26's zero-requirement install.
Do not use a combined purpose 'any maskable' icon — Chrome guidance says it degrades one context or the other; ship separate files.

keyFacts.claim: JPerm's alg data is machine-readable at https://jperm.net/lib/oll.js, pll.js, 4x4oll.js, 4x4pll.js as `algsetAlgs` arrays with {name, alg[], group, prob}; alg[0] is the recommended algorithm
keyFacts.source: https://jperm.net/lib/oll.js (downloaded and parsed: 57 OLL cases, 15 shape groups; pll.js: 21 cases)

keyFacts.claim: jperm.net/algs/f2l does not exist (404); JPerm's F2L canon is the 'Best F2L Algorithms' PDF linked from jperm.net/3x3/cfop/f2l via bit.ly/bestf2l -> Google Drive id 1nzAXYUWZJ6H2wIOXaHdWXep3W57tArbR, with Section 1 = 41 basic cases grouped by both-on-top / edge-in-slot / corner-in-slot / both-in-slot
keyFacts.source: https://jperm.net/3x3/cfop/f2l (redirect resolved via curl; PDF downloaded and text-extracted)

keyFacts.claim: Canonical 4x4 OLL parity is `Rw U2 x Rw U2 Rw U2 Rw' U2 Lw U2 Rw' U2 Rw U2 Rw' U2 Rw'` and PLL parity is `2R2 U2 2R2 Uw2 2R2 Uw2`
keyFacts.source: https://jperm.net/4x4 (verbatim grep of page HTML) and jperm.net/lib/4x4oll.js pageDetails

keyFacts.claim: JPerm's 5x5 edge parity alg is `Rw U2 x Rw U2 Rw U2 3Rw' U2 Lw U2 Rw' U2 Rw U2 Rw' U2 Rw'` — note 3Rw' where the 4x4 form has Rw'

OLL probabilities are out of 216 (51 cases 1/54, five cases 1/108 = OLL 1/21/55/56/57, one case 1/216 = OLL 20, skip 1/216) and PLL out of 72 (most 1/18; Z,E 1/36; H,Na,Nb 1/72); JPerm prob fields and CubeSkills PDFs agree exactly
keyFacts.source: jperm.net/lib/oll.js prob sum = 215/216 (computed) + https://www.cubeskills.com/uploads/pdf/tutorials/oll-algorithms.pdf and pll-algorithms.pdf (grep of per-case Probability lines)

keyFacts.claim: CubeSkills PDFs are live at cubeskills.com/uploads/pdf/tutorials/{oll-algorithms,pll-algorithms,f2l,useful-f2l-algorithms,f2l-algorithms-different-slot-positions}.pdf (all HTTP 200, application/pdf)

SpeedCubeDB covers all needed sets: /a/3x3/OLL, /a/3x3/PLL, /a/3x3/F2L (numbered F2L 1-41, F2L 1 = U R U' R'), /a/4x4/OLLParity, /a/4x4/PLLParity, /a/5x5/L2E, /a/5x5/L2C; community-vote-ranked, no public API found
keyFacts.source: https://speedcubedb.com/a/3x3/OLL and curl of /a/4x4, /a/5x5 category indexes

keyFacts.claim: SpeedCubeDB's 5x5 Last 2 Edges list has 13 cases (L2E 1-13), not 12 — e.g. L2E 4 = `Rw2 F2 U2 Rw2 U2 F2 Rw2`

Sarah Strong's 2-sided PLL recognition guide (headlights -> corner swap type, then blocks/checker/edge patterns) is at https://sarah.cubing.net/3x3x3/pll-recognition-guide and is the standard recognition-teaching reference

Yau method structure: two opposite centers -> 3 cross dedges on L -> last 4 centers -> last cross dedge -> z' + last 8 dedges -> 3x3 stage with parities; proposed by Patrick Jameson and Robert Yau 2008-09

US Copyright Office: 'Copyright does not protect facts, ideas, systems, or methods of operation, although it may protect the way these things are expressed' — algorithms are safe to use; prose/diagrams must be original
Speedsolving wiki declares no content license (MediaWiki rightsinfo API returns empty url/text) — treat its prose as all-rights-reserved, use only for terminology

cubing.js (0.63.3 current on npm) parses every jperm 3x3 alg string as-is, including 2R2, 3Rw, Uw2, M/S/E, rotations, and parenthesized groups; only the [*] parity placeholder in the 4x4 data files fails and must be expanded during extraction
keyFacts.source: local test: npm i cubing@0.63.3 + Alg round-trip of representative strings and charset scan of all 213 jperm algs

keyFacts.claim: JPerm's recommended algs are the de-facto learner standard in 2026: third-party trainers (f2l.app, f2l-trainer.top, Rouxles/Alg-Trainer) build on his sets, and SpeedCubeDB top-voted algs match his picks on flagship cases (T perm, Jb, Ua)
keyFacts.source: https://speedcubedb.com/a/3x3/OLL vote data + f2l-trainer references in speedsolving.com thread 91579

keyFacts.claim: jperm.net also hosts 2-look OLL/PLL, COLL, WV, VLS, ZBLL and 2x2 CLL/EG-1/PBL sets in the same /lib/*.js format (URLs enumerated from navbar hrefs)

risks: jperm.net /lib/*.js files are an undocumented internal format (last cache-busted 2019) — run extraction once and commit the JSON; do not fetch at build/runtime. If the format changes, the extraction script breaks loudly, not the app.

JPerm's F2L PDF has no case numbers in its extracted text and its 41-case order must be manually mapped to SpeedCubeDB's F2L 1-41 numbering — this is the highest-effort, most error-prone extraction step; budget a human verification pass (or verify each alg with the repo's cube simulator pattern applied via cubing.js KPuzzle).
SpeedCubeDB has no API and no visible content license — transcribe small factual sets (13 L2E algs) manually and cross-check only; do not bulk-scrape or mirror its vote data.
5x5 L2E is 13 cases on SpeedCubeDB, not the 12 assumed in the task brief — curriculum plan should say 13 (or explicitly define which subset it teaches).
The 4x4 and 5x5 parity algs differ by one move (Rw' vs 3Rw' in slot 7) — copy-pasting the 4x4 form into the 5x5 lesson would be wrong on a real cube; keep them as two distinct data entries.

Compilation copyright is thin but real: do not reproduce JPerm's exact page structure, description HTML, or PDF layout; re-group cases into Cubepath's own curriculum order, write all prose fresh, and self-generate every diagram (cubing.js SVG or the repo's existing Python SVG pipeline).
Speedsolving wiki content has no declared license — safe for terminology/fact checking only, never for text reuse.

Scribd/DocDroid mirrors of JPerm's PDFs are unauthorized re-uploads — always source the PDF from the official bit.ly/bestf2l Drive link, and re-verify the Drive id still resolves before the extraction run.
